response.sql: WITH per_patient AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) AS avg_igm FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_igm) AS overall_mean FROM per_patient), dev AS (SELECT pp.ID, pp.SEX, pp.avg_igm, pp.avg_igm - o.overall_mean AS deviation FROM per_patient pp CROSS JOIN overall o), sex_avg AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(deviation) AS avg_dev FROM dev GROUP BY SEX), ranked AS (SELECT d.ID, d.SEX, d.avg_igm, d.deviation, d.deviation - s.avg_dev AS excess FROM dev d JOIN sex_avg s ON s.SEX = d.SEX WHERE d.deviation > s.avg_dev) SELECT ID, SEX, avg_igm AS `aCL IgM`, deviation, excess FROM ranked ORDER BY excess IS NULL, excess DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Each examination is joined to Patient by ID with an inner join, so examinations without a matching patient are dropped. Per-patient aCL IgM is the mean of that patient's non-null examination values. Patients with no non-null aCL IgM have no value and are left out of the overall mean and the sex averages. The sex join uses = so a NULL sex matches no sex average, while a blank sex ('') forms its own group. The SQL targets SQLite (CTEs, LIMIT, boolean ORDER BY), and the NULLS-last ordering is written as ORDER BY excess IS NULL, excess DESC for portability.
